why: Gallup party identification moved from Republicans 48 Democrats 45 in the third quarter of 2024 to Democrats 50 Republicans 39 in the third quarter of 2026, 14 points toward the Democrats.
This race moves 1.01 points for every point the nation moves, so it feels about 14.1 points of that tide, a tailwind for Josh Green.

D.t: Josh Green leads by 36.1 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 165,314 votes; a one point swing is about 2,289 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +26.8 and D +45.4. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Honolulu, a projected net 107,407 votes; Hawaii, a projected net 27,845 votes; Maui, a projected net 22,599 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Josh Green runs furthest behind in Kauai, Hawaii. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 36% of voters, 58 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 1.77 points; Incomes $125K and up, 16% of voters, 62 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 0.78 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Josh Green: Immigration voters 37 to 63, White voters 58 to 42, Incomes $125K and up 62 to 38. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
